subject: Annual planning orchestration: stakeholder map + contingency scenarios
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: Annual planning orchestration: stakeholder map + contingency scenarios

Team —

Kickoff note to get annual planning and the QBR-ready narrative moving. I pulled together an initial stakeholder map and a simple scenario matrix to help us align on targets and trigger points. Attachments: stakeholder-map-v1.xlsx and scenario-matrix-template.csv.

Top asks for this week:
- Please review the stakeholder map and mark (in column D) who you want owning each decision and who needs to be informed. We need owners for: headcount buckets, price/incentive changes, dedicated capacity commitments, and regional contingencies.
- Populate a single-row, conservative/base/optimistic estimate into the scenario matrix for your org (heads + spend delta + key operational risk). Drop into the Drive folder by EOD Thu (11/12).
- Flag any blockers to the timeline below; if finance needs more time, call it out now.

Proposed timeline (compressed):
- 11/09: stakeholder map + templates (this email)
- 11/09–11/12: internal owners populate rows
- 11/16: cross-functional decision calendar sync (30m) — we will lock ranges
- 11/20–11/24: finance deep-dive and scenario stress test
- 11/30: leadership QBR doc deadline (first pass)

I’m copying Marissa as she’ll help coordinate the decision calendar and Laura for finance inputs. Vivek / Jonas — would like a quick note from you on any changes to the rollout windows or gating policy (e.g., SLA/latency SLO tradeoffs) that could materially affect timelines.

If anyone wants a 15-minute pre-brief before filling in the sheet, ping me and I’ll carve time.

Thanks —
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of GTM Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: stakeholder-map-v1.xlsx (spreadsheet stub), scenario-matrix-template.csv (csv stub)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 11:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Annual planning orchestration: stakeholder map + contingency scenarios

Thanks Vanessa — quick clarifying Qs:

1) For headcount buckets, do you want a by-role breakdown (AE/SDR/CS/Eng) or just top-line FTE numbers per org? I can do either but role-level will take more time.
2) On the scenario matrix, should we assume current pricing unchanged, or include a variant with a 10% discount assumption for renewals?

Initial thought: I’ll do a top-line FTE for GTM and add a short note for material role swaps (e.g., add two CS engineers instead of one AE). If Finance needs the role-rollup, I can follow up with a role-level file on Wed.

Jonas
Director, Product Strategy

Agree with Jonas on a pragmatic approach — top-line now, role-level if Finance pushes. Two operational notes from my side:

- Routing policy changes (region-based fallbacks) may require updating the dedicated capacity commit windows. If we push any capacity to Dedicated earlier, we should surface cost delta in the scenario matrix.
- I recommend we add a "trigger" column to the matrix (e.g., sustained latency > X ms for 7 days; ARR delta > $Yk) so decisions can be automated or prioritized.

I can drop a brief decision-calendar compact PDF that maps owner -> approval window. Will share by EOD.

Vivek
VP, Platform & Infra

All — attaching the first-pass budget assumptions (budget-assumptions-v1.xlsx). Highlights and risks:

- Revenue upside in optimistic case assumes 12% higher average deal size from upsells and new seat pricing; please annotate where that is unlikely.
- We need headcount detail for any >3 FTE changes per org so we can model benefits, ramp, and hiring cadence. Jonas — if you can add a role-level supplement for large changes that would be helpful.
- CapEx: any dedicated capacity commits should include estimated GPU-months and expected amortization window — Vivek, can infra provide quick kernel for GPU-month estimates?

I’ll also add a finance 'confidence' column in the scenario matrix to capture how reliable each estimate is.

Laura Bennett
Finance Partner, GTM

Appreciate the fast responses. Quick updates:

- Jonas: top-line FTE is fine for the 11/12 drop; please mark any >3 changes for follow-up.
- Vivek: good call on trigger column; I added that to the scenario-matrix-template.csv. The decision-calendar-compact.pdf will be in Drive by EOD.
- Laura: finance confidence column is great — please surface any line items that require board approval.

I scheduled the 11/16 30-minute sync (invite attached in calendar link). Agenda: alignment on owners, lock ranges for base/conservative/optimistic, and decide if we need an external stress-test session with Forge Partners.

Also, Marissa — please confirm who owns the QBR doc draft (slides + narrative). I propose Product owns the roadmap slide and GTM owns targets and go-to-market asks.

Vanessa

Attachments: decision-calendar-compact.pdf (pdf stub)
